claimed_purpose.text: Reveals a gap in current evaluations by showing that agents with near-saturated performance on existing long-context memory benchmarks perform poorly in the agentic setting.
MemoryArena is designed to benchmark agent memory in interdependent multi-session agentic tasks.

mechanisms.text: Progressive Search answers are structured dicts with a target ASIN and attributes list, indicating product-retrieval grading.

ledger.claim: Agents with near-saturated performance on LoCoMo perform poorly on MemoryArena, exposing a gap in current evaluations.
ledger.quote: reveals that agents with near-saturated performance on existing long-context memory benchmarks like LoCoMo perform poorly in our agentic setting, exposing a gap in current evaluations for agents with memory
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: The benchmark evaluates agent memory by requiring agents to carry context (background information) across interdependent subtasks within each agentic task.
ledger.quote: This dataset contains structured multi-session agentic tasks with question [list], answer [list] with necessary background context. Each row in the jsonl represents a agentic task [dict] with multiple subtasks, their corresponding answers, and background information.

ledger.claim: MemoryArena contains 766 total tasks with average 6.9 interdependent subtasks per task and average 57 action steps per task.
ledger.quote: MemoryArena: 766 [tasks], 6.9 [avg interdependent subtasks], 57 [avg steps]
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Task Progress Score (PS) is defined as the fraction of subtasks passed within a task, averaged over all tasks: PS = (1/N) * sum_i (|s_i^pass| / |S_i|).
ledger.quote: PS_{S_i} = |s_i^{pass}| / |S_i|, PS = (1/N) * sum_i^N PS_{S_i}
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Task Success Rate (SR) measures the percentage of tasks fully solved.
ledger.quote: We also report the Task Success Rate (SR), which measures the percentage of tasks that are fully solved.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Math Formal Reasoning has 40 tasks, 2–16 subtasks, average trace length 18.1k tokens; Physics has 20 tasks, 2–12 subtasks, average trace length 14.1k tokens.
ledger.quote: Math Formal Reasoning: 2 [min ST], 16 [max ST], 18.1k [avg T. trace L], 40 [# T]; Phys. Formal Reasoning: 2 [min ST], 12 [max ST], 14.1k [avg T. trace L], 20 [# T]
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: All methods achieve low SR and PS overall; Group Travel Planning yields near-zero SR and PS for all methods; best single-task SR is achieved in Formal Reasoning (Physics) by text-embedding-3-small at 0.7.
ledger.quote: Overall, all methods achieve low SR and PS, with two environments exhibiting near-zero SR, indicating that MemoryArena poses a challenging evaluation setting.
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Bundled Web Shopping tasks include 1 ground truth item, 2 compatible distractors, and 2 incompatible distractors per session (5 candidates total, order shuffled).
ledger.quote: With 3 compatible candidates (1 target item and 2 compatible distractors) identified... We selected 2 items that are logically compatible... We selected 2 items that are logically mutually exclusive... to serve as 'hard negative' samples
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Progressive Web Search uses OpenAI text-embedding-3 for semantic retrieval with top-k=5 results, each truncated to 512 tokens, during evaluation.
ledger.quote: the agent uses OpenAI's retriever backend and the text-embedding-3 model to encode queries and documents for semantic search. The retriever tool is set to retrieve the top k=5 search results, where each result is truncated to the first 512 token of the corresponding document.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Formal Reasoning experiments use temperature=0, max output tokens=8192, and require symbolic results in LaTeX for reproducibility.
ledger.quote: set the maximum output to 8192... We use a temperature of 0 to guarantee reproducibility. We also requires symbolic results output in LaTex.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Experiments run on official OpenAI API, Anthropic API, and Vertex AI APIs; GPU experiments use NVIDIA H100.
ledger.quote: All of our experiments run with official OpenAI API, Anthropic API, and Vertex AI APIs. For experiments that need to run on GPU, we use NVIDIA H100 GPUs.
ledger.label: unknown
